allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

versioning.description: Versioning scheme applied to spec artifacts. Decision rule: use 'semver' for public APIs or schemas with explicit breaking-change semantics (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); use 'date-based' for internal artifact versioning where freshness matters more than compatibility (YYYY-MM-DD); use 'sequential' for simple monotonic increment when breaking changes are managed out-of-band. Examples: public REST API → 'semver'; internal spec artifacts → 'date-based'. Anti-pattern: using 'sequential' for public APIs (consumers cannot determine breaking changes from the version number alone).

pr_rules.description: Pull request rules governing how spec changes are submitted, reviewed, and merged. Decision matrix for which rules to include: always include 'validate-all' (mandatory for every PR touching spec files). Include conditionally: 'matrix' (when traceability links changed — new FR/API pairs), 'fixtures-lint' (when fixture targets changed), 'canonical-lint'/'canonical-integrity' (when canon entries were added or modified), 'security' (when auth, PII handling, or threat model changed), 'hallucination-lint' (when new spec content was added from AI generation), 'seed-lint' (when seed document references changed). Anti-pattern: including all 13 rules for every PR regardless of what changed — this makes CI slow and signals that the rules are not being considered.

items.description: A single CI/governance check required on pull requests. Selection guide: always include 'validate-all' (schema validation of all spec files) and 'governance-check' (commit message pattern enforcement). Add 'matrix' when FR, NFR, or API traceability links change. Add 'test' and 'build' for repos containing implementation code alongside the spec. Add 'canonical-lint' when canonical registry changes are expected. Add 'security' for production services handling PII or payment data. Add 'audit' for regulated environments requiring immutable evidence. Anti-pattern: including 'deploy' in a spec-only repo — deploy rules belong in the CI gates spec (Step 12).

spec_first_policy.description: Enforces the spec-first rule: spec artifacts must be updated and merged before corresponding implementation code is written. When true, PRs that introduce new code without a preceding spec change will be blocked by governance-check.

commit_message_rules.description: Rules governing commit message format and content. Validated by governance-check on every PR. Defines the regex pattern and artifact ID requirements that keep commits traceable to spec changes.

require_spec_ids.description: When set to true, governance-check enforces that every commit message must embed at least one bracketed spec artifact ID (e.g., [fr-user-login]). When false, IDs are optional. Valid spec ID prefixes that may appear in commit messages: fr-* (functional requirements), api-* (API contracts), cap-* (capabilities), nfr-* (non-functional requirements), inv-* (invariants), fix-* (fixtures), ms-* (milestones), ext-* (extensions). The governance-check command validates that commit messages reference IDs that exist in the spec. Anti-pattern: referencing a spec ID prefix not in this list (e.g., req-*, feat-*) — use the canonical prefixes so cross-step traceability works.

pattern.description: Commit message pattern that governance-check validates. Should include step reference in brackets: 'feat(spec): add login flow [fr-user-login]' — enforced at runtime by governance-check. The bracketed IDs should match valid artifact IDs in the spec. Conventional Commits format is recommended: '<type>(<scope>): <summary> [<artifact-id>]'.

id_pattern_ref.description: Canonical reference to the ID pattern used in commit messages. Kind must be 'action' or 'term'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:action:governance-check", "kind": "action", "label": "governance-check"}. References the canonical entry for the commit ID pattern enforced by this governance rule. Omit if the pattern is fully defined by the 'pattern' field without a canonical vocabulary reference.

error_message.description: Human-readable rejection message shown when a commit fails pattern validation. Should list the allowed commit types and provide a valid example. Example: 'Commit must match: feat|fix|chore|docs(spec): description [artifact-id]. Example: feat(spec): add login flow [fr-user-login]'.

review_policy.description: Policy governing spec review requirements and evidence collection. Specifies what reviewers must verify (verdict_requirements), what metadata must accompany each review, and which evidence sources are acceptable at each deployment phase.

verdict_requirements.description: Concrete, checkable conditions that reviewers must verify before approving a spec change. Each item should be a specific, testable condition — not a vague quality aspiration. Examples: 'All referenced IDs exist in their source spec files', 'Changelog entry present for breaking changes', 'New FRs have at least 2 acceptance criteria'. Should be achievable by a reviewer in under 5 minutes per item.

items.description: A single verdict requirement — a specific, falsifiable condition an approver must confirm before approving. Write as an affirmative declarative sentence that can be checked off. Examples: 'All fr-* IDs referenced in the changed artifact exist in spec/04_fr_list.json', 'No capability has been removed without a corresponding out_of_scope entry in the charter', 'All trace links in the changed artifact resolve to existing upstream IDs'. Anti-pattern: 'Review quality of the spec' — verdicts must be checkable without subjective judgment.

required_metadata.description: Field names that every review submission must include (e.g., 'reviewer_id', 'review_date', 'evidence_link'). Acts as a checklist enforcing consistent review records.

evidence_source_by_phase.description: Maps each deployment phase to the authoritative evidence source that satisfies review for that phase. Ensures reviewers know which artifact or system to consult at dev, staging, and production.

dev.description: Evidence source accepted during the development phase. Dev phase evidence = automatically generated outputs from the developer's local or CI run: 'unit-test-report', 'lint-report', 'type-check-output'. Examples: 'unit-test-report', 'lint-report'. Anti-pattern: 'manual-review', 'slack-approval' (not reproducible artifacts); 'all-tests-pass' (not a named artifact).

staging.description: Evidence source accepted during the staging phase. Staging phase evidence = outputs from the integration CI pipeline: 'ci-pipeline-output', 'integration-test-report', 'smoke-test-results', 'coverage-report'. Examples: 'integration-test-report', 'smoke-test-results'. Anti-pattern: staging evidence that is the same as dev evidence (staging should include higher-level integration tests).

prod.description: Evidence source required before production deployment. Prod phase evidence = formal sign-off artifacts: 'qa-sign-off', 'penetration-test-report', 'load-test-report', 'security-scan-report'. At least one human approval artifact is typically required for prod phase. Examples: 'qa-sign-off', 'penetration-test-report'. Anti-pattern: prod evidence that is identical to staging (production gating should be stricter).

reviewers.description: GitHub handles or team names of designated reviewers responsible for approving spec changes. Decision rule: use '@username' for individual reviewers when specific domain expertise is required; use '@org/team-name' for team reviews when any member of the team can approve. Use team handle when 3 or more members could validly review; use individual handle only for unique expertise (e.g., a specific security engineer for PII policy review). Examples: '@acme/platform-team', '@alice', '@acme/security-team'. Anti-pattern: email addresses ('alice@company.com'), full names without @ prefix, empty array for production gates.

trace.description: Traceability links connecting this governance spec to upstream artifacts. Governance artifacts trace using three types: 'depends_on' (this governance rule only activates when the referenced FR or cap is in scope), 'verified_by' (the referenced artifact provides evidence that this governance requirement is met), 'derives_from' (the governance rule was derived from the referenced charter or policy). Example: [{"type": "depends_on", "id": "fr-user-login", "note": "Authentication governance applies only when auth FRs are in scope"}]. Every governance rule should trace to its origin; un-traced rules cannot be validated against charter scope.

items.description: A single traceability reference for this governance spec. Common types at step 10: 'depends_on' for invariants or policies this governance enforces; 'verified_by' for CI gate IDs that verify compliance; 'derives_from' for charter sections that mandate this governance approach. Example: {"type": "verified_by", "id": "gate-governance-check", "note": "Governance rules enforced by this CI gate on every PR"}. Anti-pattern: omitting the 'note' field on governance traces — unannoted governance links cannot be audited.

links.description: External links to governance resources — wikis, runbooks, branch protection settings, or policy documents that supplement this spec.

items.description: A link to an external governance resource. Include a 'rel' that describes the resource's relationship to this spec (e.g., 'branch-protection-rules', 'codeowners-file').

policy_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance policy in the canonical registry. Kind must be 'risk_category' or 'capability'. Decision rule: use kind='risk_category' when the policy is about risk mitigation (e.g., security policy → {"id": "cn:core:risk_category:authn", "kind": "risk_category", "label": "authn"}). Use kind='capability' when the policy is about a system capability constraint (e.g., deployment policy → {"id": "cn:project:capability:continuous-deployment", "kind": "capability", "label": "continuous-deployment"}). Reference the canonical entry that represents the governance framework this spec enforces. Validated by canonical-integrity lint. Anti-pattern: using kind='term' — governance policies must reference either a risk category or a capability.

command_ref.description: Canonical reference to the CLI command this governance rule triggers. Kind must be 'action'. Reference the canonical command this governance rule triggers. Example: {"id": "cn:core:capability:governance-check", "kind": "capability", "label": "governance-check"} for the specdev governance-check command. Omit when the governance rule does not map to an automated command. Validated by canonical-integrity lint. Anti-pattern: fabricating a command_ref ID — only reference commands that exist in the canon.
